source_refs.note: Topic 2.8.1.1 Defining Classes and Creating Objects (PDF 57-58, printed 54-55). The printed __init__ line is garbled and describe() returns a tuple; the lesson uses a working f-string version. Recorded.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
class ToyCar:
....def __init__(self, color, size, wheels):
........self.color = color
........self.size = size
........self.wheels = wheels

....def describe(self):
........return f"This toy car is {self.color}, {self.size} and has {self.wheels} wheels."

car1 = ToyCar("red", "small", 4)
car2 = ToyCar("blue", "large", 6)
print(car1.describe())
print(car2.describe())

items: Class definition: ToyCar is the template, describing the attributes color, size and wheels.
Creating objects: car1 and car2 are particular toy cars made from the template, each with its own attributes.
Using methods: describe() returns a description of the car.
self: refers to the particular object inside its methods.

blocks.explanation: "This toy car is blue, large and has 6 wheels."

items: class ToyCar with __init__(self, ...) sets attributes; objects ToyCar(...); methods use self.
